land.text: the satrapy of Caria, held by Hecatomnus

predecessors.note: Hecatomnus 'became satrap of Caria c. 395 - c. 392 BCE' and was 'in office by 392 BCE'; the Hecatomnids stayed Persian satraps with 'considerable autonomy'.

land.text: Caria taken by Alexander in 334 ('Alexander captures Caria'), with Ada reinstated as its ruler; Lycia and the islands followed

successors.note: The Hecatomnid table gives Ada I a second rule 'c. 334 to c. 320s'; the state ends here with the conquest.

capitals.name: Mylasa (Milas)
capitals.note: The Mausolus page: the seat moved from Mylasa to Halicarnassus 'early in their reign'.

capitals.name: Halicarnassus (Bodrum)
capitals.note: Moved by Mausolus and Artemisia early in their joint reign (from 377); no year on the page. Halicarnassus was held by Orontobates against Alexander in 334.

rulers.name: Hecatomnus
rulers.title: satrap
rulers.note: 'satrap of Caria c. 395 - c. 392 BCE', 'in office by 392 BCE'; the dynasty table gives c. 395 to c. 377.

rulers.name: Mausolus
rulers.title: satrap
rulers.note: Succeeded in 377/6; died 353/2 (Mausolus page); ruled with his sister-wife Artemisia II.

rulers.name: Artemisia II
rulers.title: satrap
rulers.note: 'ruled alone for two years until c. 351/0 BCE'.

rulers.name: Idrieus (with Ada I)
rulers.title: satrap
rulers.note: Idrieus died c. 344/3; Ada then became sole ruler.

rulers.name: Pixodarus
rulers.title: satrap
rulers.note: Ruled 'until c. 335 BCE' (table); the Siege of Halicarnassus page: Darius then appointed Orontobates, a Persian, satrap.

rulers.name: Orontobates
rulers.title: satrap (Persian appointee)
rulers.note: Held Halicarnassus against Alexander in 334 with Memnon of Rhodes (Siege of Halicarnassus page); the Hecatomnid line was interrupted.

correction.text: the satrapy of Caria under Hecatomnus and, from 377, Mausolus

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; the Achaemenid Empire shape of 340 includes Caria inside its 4.03 M km2). The pages give no boundary and no area; the Caria region (70 cells, about 17,700 km2) is the satrapy.

correction.text: Caria and Lycia, 'given' to Mausolus after the Revolt of the Satraps was 'squashed in 362/1 BCE'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Lycia added. The Hecatomnid page says only 'after the Revolt of the Satraps'; the Mausolus page gives the 362/1 end of the revolt.

correction.text: Caria, Lycia, and Rhodes with the other Dodecanese islands, gained after the Social War

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Rhodes and the Dodecanese added after the Social War (ended 355). The pages do not say when the islands or Lycia were lost; the shape holds to 334 (confidence 1 for 350-335) because Alexander's conquest is the next dated change.

region.text: the satrapy of Caria, with Mylasa as seat

ledger.note: 392: Hecatomnus is satrap of Caria. 'Hecatomnus therefore became satrap of Caria c. 395 - c. 392 BCE' and was 'in office by 392 BCE'. The dynasty runs from him to Ada I and ends with Alexander.
392: the Hecatomnids hold Caria as Persian satraps 'under the Achaemenid Empire, although they ruled with considerable autonomy'.

377: Mausolus and Artemisia move the seat from Mylasa to Halicarnassus. The Mausolus page says 'early in their reign' (it began 377) and gives no year; Mausolus 'became satrap when his father Hecatomnus died in 377/6 BCE'.

362: Mausolus is given Lycia. 'He remained in office after the revolt was squashed in 362/1 BCE' and was 'then given Lycia to govern'; he had sided with Artaxerxes in the Revolt of the Satraps (siege of Adramyttium, 366). The Lycian dynasts are not named on the page.

region.text: Rhodes and the other Dodecanese islands

ledger.note: 355: Rhodes and the Dodecanese come under Mausolus after the Social War. The Hecatomnid page lists Caria, Lycia, and Rhodes with other Dodecanese islands among the dynasty's lands, the islands gained after the Social War against Athens; the Social War 'ended quickly in 355 BCE' (Mausolus page: Rhodes, Chios and Byzantium 'rebelled against Athens in 357 BCE', backed by Mausolus and Artemisia). The page gives no year for the islands themselves.

334: Alexander besieges Halicarnassus. The siege 'was fought between Alexander the Great and the Achaemenid Persian Empire in 334 BC'; Orontobates and Memnon of Rhodes 'entrenched themselves in Halicarnassus'; Ada, in the fortress of Alinda, surrendered it to him.
334: Alexander captures Caria (infobox 'Alexander captures Caria', undated within the page) and commits the government to Ada, who 'formally adopted Alexander as her son'.
334: Caria passes to Alexander. 'Alexander captures Caria' (infobox); Ada keeps its government under him.
334: Lycia and the Dodecanese pass to Alexander's sphere. Page silent: neither the Siege of Halicarnassus nor the Hecatomnid page dates their end under the dynasty; bridged to the conquest.
334: the Persian overlordship of Caria ends with Alexander's conquest ('Alexander captures Caria').
334: the Hecatomnid state ends. 'Alexander the Great entered Anatolia in 334 BCE'; Ada I was installed as queen after Orontobates was ousted, her second rule c. 334 to the 320s (the dynasty table).

wars.name: Revolt of the Satraps (Mausolus on the king's side)
wars.outcome: Mausolus sided mainly with Artaxerxes and in 366 'led the siege of Adramyttium' at the king's request with Autophradates; the revolt was squashed in 362/1 and he was given Lycia.
wars.note: The page says the revolt occurred 'mostly during the 360s BCE'.

wars.name: Social War (357-355 BC)
wars.outcome: Rhodes, Chios and Byzantium 'rebelled against Athens in 357 BCE' with Mausolus and Artemisia behind them; 'The Social War ended quickly in 355 BCE'. Rhodes and the Dodecanese then count among the dynasty's lands (Hecatomnid page).

wars.name: Siege of Halicarnassus
wars.outcome: Alexander captured Caria; Ada, who held Alinda, surrendered it to him and was left the government of Caria.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for the satrapy or the Dodecanese holdings; Lycia and the islands may have been lost before 334 (page silent).

sources.title: Hecatomnid dynasty
sources.note: Dynasty table, satrap status, lands (Caria, Lycia, Rhodes, Dodecanese), Alexander 334.

sources.title: Mausolus
sources.note: 377/6 accession, Revolt of the Satraps 366-362/1, Lycia, Social War 357-355, death 353/2, capital move undated.

sources.title: Siege of Halicarnassus
sources.note: Alexander, Orontobates, Memnon, Ada at Alinda, 334.

notes: Three pages (budget 2-5). No Cliopatria row: Caria lies inside the Achaemenid Empire shape, and the achaemenid-empire dossier does not show the satrapy as a unit. This dossier is a dynasty of satraps with autonomy, drawn as a vassal tint of the Achaemenids (vassal pair in its own ledger, the Cappadocia convention). Unsettled: the start (c. 395 or 392) and the end of the dynasty's line (the table runs Ada I to the 320s); when Lycia and the islands were lost; the capital move year. Not opened: Caria, Idrieus, Pixodarus, Social War pages. Capital coordinates (Milas, Bodrum) are standard values, not from the pages. Rhodes in 355: rhodes (eu-02-b) has no event for the Carian period. If macedonian-empire wants Ada's second reign (334-320s) as a vassal, it should add it.
